title: Stone, Rock, Clay, Dust, Ash, Mud & Soil — Material-State Grammar
status: material metaphor + biblical context + project transformation grammar
purpose: Separate durable solids, formable earth, fine particulate, combustion residue, wet unresolved mixture and living substrate so the project's lower/material symbols can transform without becoming a single moralized 'mud' category.
master_rule: Material state precedes moral value. A thing can be below, broken, dusty, muddy, stony or ashy without being evil. Ask what properties and transitions matter.

states.distinction: Rock is a material/landform category; Cornerstone is an architectural role.
Cornerstone meaning depends on building practice/textual metaphor; it is not every important stone.

states.scholarly_context: Jewish texts could combine Genesis dust-creation and prophetic potter/clay traditions as related but distinct creation/formability images.
states.distinction: Clay is not simply hardened mud and is not stone without geological/ceramic transformation.
Dust is not Soil; dust lacks the living ecological structure implied by healthy soil.

states.biblical_neighbor: Numbers 19 uses burned red-heifer ash mixed with water in corpse-impurity purification ritual.
states.distinction: Ash is not automatically fertile, pure or dead; composition and context matter.
Mud is not Swamp: Mud is material/state; Swamp is terrain/regime of accumulated entanglement.
Soil is not purity; healthy soil contains decomposed history and complex living/nonliving matter.

transition_grammar.condition: water, shaping, drying and possibly firing depending material/product
transition_grammar.boundary: This is not a universal spiritual sequence.

transition_grammar.project_neighbor: destruction or transformation leaves recoverable residue

transition_grammar.boundary: Literal ash can harm soils at high concentration or unsuitable chemistry; project 'Ash→Soil' is primarily a repair metaphor.
Not a geological mechanism; biblical kingdom imagery.

project_cycle.sequence: Dust/raw material → mixture/Mud → {capture/Swamp | shaping/Clay | contextualization/Soil} → Root/Seed → Tree/Fruit; rupture may create Ash that re-enters the fork.
project_cycle.correction: Do not force every material through every state. This is a routing grammar, not one universal lifecycle.

moral_boundary: Softness can enable formation or create instability.
Residue can preserve evidence or contaminate.
Burial/depth can nourish roots or conceal harm.
Only downstream function, relation and Fruit determine project valence.
